title: Maize domestication in the Central Balsas Valley
summary: Excavations at the Xihuatoxtla Shelter in the Central Balsas watershed of Guerrero, Mexico, found maize starch grains and phytoliths on stone tools dated to at least about 8,700 calendar years ago, the earliest maize evidence known when published in 2009.

uncertainty.note: Charcoal dated 8990-8610 cal BP; the authors quote "at least 8700 calendrical years BP" (year = 1950 minus cal BP). Maize remains occur at and below the dated level, so the true domestication date is earlier than the dated horizon.

as_recorded.calendar: Calendar years before present (cal BP, 1950), radiocarbon
as_recorded.value: 8990-8610 cal B.P. (7920 +/- 40 B.P.) for the charcoal; stone tools dated to at least 8700 calendrical years B.P.
maize domesticated from its wild ancestor more than 8700 years ago

where.modern_name: Xihuatoxtla Shelter, near Iguala, Guerrero, Mexico (GeoNames fix is for nearby Barranca Xihuatoxtla, 260 m from the shelter)
where.historical_name: No polity; preceramic hunter-gatherer-cultivator landscape of the Central Balsas watershed

importance.justification: Maize became a staple of the Americas; the site gives the earliest known evidence of its domestication and points to the seasonal tropical forest of southwestern Mexico as its origin.

sources.title: The cultural and chronological context of early Holocene maize and squash domestication in the Central Balsas River Valley, Mexico (PNAS 106:5014-5018)
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (via PubMed Central)
sources.author: Anthony J. Ranere, Dolores R. Piperno, Irene Holst, Ruth Dickau, Jose Iriarte

sources.title: Maize domesticated more than 8,700 years ago in Mexico (research release)
